thread:
alex: Heads-up — post-merge alerts from the runtime release. CI perf check failed and we started seeing KV-cache-related OOMs on canary nodes.
priya: saw the same in prod-canary, tail latency spiked ~40% for long sequences and some tasks hit OOM during token generation.
sam: CI job: `ci-perf-check/runtime-e2e` failed with latency regression. Screenshot of perf dashboard attached.
marta: stack traces point to `kv_cache::eviction::policy` churn after commit 4f8d2a7 — that patch changed eviction ordering to MRU-first for small sequences.
ci-bot: [alert] perf-check/runtime-e2e failed 1718205400: tail_latency_p95 +45% vs baseline. See https://ci.internal/reports/1718205400
oncall-ingest: memory graphs from canary nodes: resident_size climbs linearly until OOM. jemalloc stats show fragmentation ratio jumped from 1.08 -> 1.5.
alex: quick bisect. I ran `git bisect start -- bad v2026.03.15 -- good v2026.03.10` then tested locally on small reproducer.
alex: git bisect output snippet:
```
$ git bisect run ./scripts/repro-kv-oom.sh
4f8d2a7c3a1bad64c9c2a5f2b7d5e9a1f2b3c4d5 is the first bad commit
```
priya: that matches my manual inspection. The 4f8d2a7 change touches `LRUCache::insert` and `evict_candidates` and the change replaced a size-based threshold with a window-based heuristic.
sam: profiling flamegraph (short sequences) shows a hot path in `kv_cache::lookup` spending more time on list re-ordering. Link: https://profiles.internal/flame/1718205
marta: repro script I used (short):
```
#!/bin/bash
for n in {1..200}; do
  ./runtime --model gpt-medium --seq-len 4096 --prompt-size 512 >/dev/null &
done
sleep 60
```
priya: running that locally reproduces OOM on commit 4f8d2a7 but not on previous. Heap dump attached: top consumers are cache shard metadata + fragmented arenas.
oncall-ingest: jemalloc `mallctl` metrics attached: `stats.allocated` stable, `stats.mapped` increases, `stats.active` diverges — consistent with fragmentation due to frequent small allocations from eviction list nodes.
alex: are we sure it's the eviction heuristic and not a regression in the way we serialize cache entries? The commit also refactored `CacheEntry` layout.
marta: I compared struct layouts: padding changed, `last_accessed` moved which increased per-entry size by 8 bytes. When multiplied by millions of entries that explains extra resident, but not the fragmentation spike. The window heuristic increases churn leading to many short-lived allocations which triggers fragmentation.
sam: CI reproducible test: added a perf gate in `ci/perf/runtime_kv_eviction_test` which runs the repro workload and checks memory delta < 1.2x. It failed on the PR that merged 4f8d2a7.
priya: for immediate mitigation I propose reverting the eviction heuristic part while keeping the layout improvements if possible. Revert patch candidate: commit `r: 8a9b7c1` which reverts 4f8d2a7's eviction logic.
alex: agreed, mark rollout as blocker. @deploy-bot please hold canary rollout for runtime until revert lands.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout paused by alex (reason: perf/oom regressions).
ci-bot: created rollback PR draft: https://git.internal/runtime/pulls/432-revert-eviction-heuristic (CI triggered).
priya: added a unit test to simulate heavy eviction churn and assert fragmentation stays below threshold. Pushed to the revert PR.
sam: note: we should also add jemalloc stats to the perf dashboard for future runs (active/mapped/dirty) — will open a follow-up.
marta: after applying revert candidate on canary, memory stabilized within 10 minutes and p95 latency returned to baseline. Verified with same repro script.
alex: excellent. Let's keep the layout change but avoid immediate allocation churn — possible approaches: use object pooling for eviction nodes, or change to index-based free lists.
priya: pooling looks simplest for a quick follow-up. I'll prototype an object pool for eviction nodes and run the perf job.
oncall-ingest: logs: `oom: allocation failed: arena 3 exhausted` -> after revert those logs ceased.
sam: CI run for the revert PR passed perf-check for the kv test; full e2e still running but so far green.
priya: recording the root cause for postmortem: (1) struct layout + (2) eviction heuristic increased short-lived allocations -> fragmentation -> increased mapped memory -> OOM under long sequences.
mart a: action items:
- revert eviction heuristic (PR 432) — DONE
- add jemalloc metrics to perf dashboard — sam
- add pooled allocations for eviction nodes — priya prototype
- add regression test in CI for kv churn — sam merged test

alex: thanks everyone. After revert we'll coordinate a careful re-introduction behind a feature flag and stress-test with long sequences (>=4096).
priya: note to self: when reintroducing, also run with `--jemalloc.opt background_thread:true` variations, fragmentation sensitive.
sam: will follow up with a retrospective note in #postmortems once the rollback fully clears. :thumbsup:
ci-bot: perf-check/runtime-e2e for PR 432: PASS (p95 within baseline).
deploy-bot: canary resumed after manual approval by alex.
priya: closing loop — prod didn't hit OOM due to canary hold, thanks for quick triage.
marta: leaving a short write-up in the eng-runtime wiki with reproduction steps and mitigation notes.
alex: good job everyone. We'll keep the revert PR open until pooled allocator lands.
